components.label: Config Server
components.purpose: Spring Cloud Config Server on port 8888. Every other Spring service (and the discovery server) imports its configuration from it at startup.

components.label: Discovery Server (Eureka)
components.purpose: Eureka server on port 8761 where services register and where the gateway looks up instances by name. Runs standalone (does not register with itself or fetch a registry).

components.label: Admin Server (Spring Boot Admin)
components.purpose: Spring Boot Admin server on port 9090. It is also an Eureka discovery client.

components.label: Tracing Server (Zipkin)
components.purpose: Zipkin, run from the stock openzipkin/zipkin image in docker-compose, port 9411. Services export spans to it.

components.label: Prometheus
components.purpose: Prometheus image built from docker/prometheus with the repo's prometheus.yml; container port 9090 published as 9091.

components.label: Grafana
components.purpose: Grafana image built from docker/grafana with provisioned datasource and a petclinic dashboard; container port 3000 published as 3030.

components.label: Config repo
components.purpose: Second git repository holding the configuration the Config Server serves: a shared application.yml plus one YAML file per service name.

flows.title: Service startup
flows.summary: How customers-service starts in docker-compose: the config server comes up first, then the service imports its configuration (served from the config repo), registers with Eureka, and the gateway later resolves lb://customers-service.

steps.label: Config server starts and becomes healthy
steps.description: Port 8888; its compose healthcheck curls http://config-server:8888 (10 retries every 5s). Because the image runs with the docker profile and the native profile is not enabled, the git uri backend is the one configured.

steps.label: Discovery server starts after config-server is healthy
steps.description: depends_on config-server with condition service_healthy; its own healthcheck curls port 8761.

steps.label: Wait for config-server and discovery-server to be healthy
steps.description: depends_on lists both with service_healthy; the container then starts with the docker profile (port 8081).

steps.label: Import configuration for customers-service
steps.description: spring.config.import in the docker profile is configserver:http://config-server:8888; outside docker it is optional:configserver:${CONFIG_SERVER_URL:http://localhost:8888/}. spring.application.name is customers-service.

steps.label: Read config files from the git backend
steps.description: The git uri points at the spring-petclinic-microservices-config repository, default label main. The repo holds application.yml (shared) and customers-service.yml.

steps.label: Shared and per-service YAML
steps.description: Shared application.yml sets random port 0 and the docker-profile zipkin endpoint; customers-service.yml has a docker-profile block with port 8081 and the Eureka defaultZone.

steps.label: Configuration properties
steps.description: customers-service now has server.port 8081, eureka.client.serviceUrl.defaultZone and the zipkin endpoint from the config repo.

steps.label: Register with Eureka as customers-service
steps.description: Eureka client enabled by @EnableDiscoveryClient; the registry URL is the defaultZone from the config repo.

steps.label: Resolve lb://customers-service
steps.description: A gateway route for Path=/api/customer/** has target uri lb://customers-service; the gateway is a discovery client with a load-balanced client.

steps.label: Registered instance(s) of customers-service
steps.description: Eureka registry answer; the gateway forwards to the returned instance.

items.text: Java 17 is the project Java version, and CI builds with JDK 17.
Maven multi-module build: a parent pom of packaging pom lists eight modules (admin, customers, vets, visits, genai, config, discovery, api-gateway).
Spring Boot 4.0.1 parent with Spring Cloud 2025.1.0.
CI is a GitHub Actions workflow that runs a Maven package build on push and pull request to main.
Docker images are built with the buildDocker Maven profile (./mvnw clean install -P buildDocker) from one shared docker/Dockerfile and tagged springcommunity/<artifactId>.
The shared Dockerfile is a two-stage build on eclipse-temurin:17 that extracts Spring Boot layers and starts with JarLauncher; it sets SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=docker.

docker-compose.yml runs config-server, discovery-server, customers, visits, vets, genai, api-gateway, tracing-server (zipkin), admin-server, grafana-server and prometheus-server. Databases are not part of compose.

Startup order: discovery-server waits for a healthy config-server; customers, visits, vets, genai, api-gateway and admin-server wait for both config-server and discovery-server to be healthy (depends_on condition service_healthy). Tracing, Grafana and Prometheus have no depends_on.

Published ports: api-gateway 8080, customers 8081, visits 8082, vets 8083, genai 8084, config-server 8888, discovery-server 8761, admin-server 9090, zipkin 9411, Grafana 3030 (container 3000), Prometheus 9091 (container 9090).
Every compose container has a memory limit (512M for the Java services and Zipkin, 256M for Grafana and Prometheus).

Each service imports its config with spring.config.import: optional:configserver:${CONFIG_SERVER_URL:http://localhost:8888/} by default and configserver:http://config-server:8888 under the docker profile.
Config server serves from the git repo spring-petclinic-microservices-config (default label main). Setting the native profile and GIT_REPO switches to a local file-system backend.

evidence.quote: Use the File System Backend to avoid git pulling

items.text: The config repo has a shared application.yml plus one file per service name (admin-server, api-gateway, customers-service, discovery-server, genai-service, tracing-server, vets-service, visits-service).
By default services start on a random port (server.port 0); the docker profile in each service's file fixes the port.

evidence.quote: start services on random port by default

items.text: Spring profiles: docker (set in the Dockerfile), mysql (switches datasource to a MySQL URL and the db/mysql scripts, in the shared config), chaos-monkey (enables Chaos Monkey; run_all.sh --chaos-monkey passes it), native (config-server file backend).
Shared config exposes all actuator endpoints and enables the Prometheus metrics export; the Zipkin endpoint under the docker profile is http://tracing-server:9411/api/v2/spans.
Prometheus scrapes itself and four services (api-gateway, customers, visits, vets) at /actuator/prometheus; genai-service and admin-server are not listed.
